name: Risks of Owner‑Builder Permits for LA County Kitchen Overhauls

mainEntity.name: What are the risks of hiring a kitchen overhauling contractor in Los Angeles County who asks me to pull the permits as an owner‑builder?
mainEntity.text: What are the risks of hiring a kitchen overhauling contractor in Los Angeles County who asks me to pull the permits as an owner‑builder?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some contractors in Los Angeles County may encourage you to act as the owner‑builder and pull permits yourself, often suggesting it will save money. In reality, doing so transfers many responsibilities and risks from the contractor to you. As owner‑builder, you may be viewed by regulators and insurers as the general contractor, responsible for code compliance, worker safety, and coordination of subs and inspections. If problems arise with workmanship or unpermitted changes, enforcement agencies may come to you first. Future buyers, appraisers, or lenders might also question work done under your name rather than a licensed contractor’s. You may face challenges if you try to claim against a contractor’s license or insurance when they were not officially listed on the permit. Additionally, handling inspections, corrections, and plan changes is more complex without the contractor in the official role. If a contractor insists on this arrangement, ask why they are unwilling to pull permits under their license and consider it a red flag. For most homeowners, hiring a licensed kitchen overhauling contractor who pulls permits directly is a safer, more transparent approach.
